result.title: Structured Relevance Determination and Channel Additive Gaussian Processes for Image Data
result.summary: We introduce radial basis function (RBF) kernels for Gaussian processes that use structured hyperparameter sharing for image-valued inputs. For high-dimensional inputs such as images, a fully anisotropic RBF kernel assigns a separate lengthscale to each input dimension, which can introduce many hyperparameters and may lead to overfitting and poorly calibrated predictive uncertainty when data are limited. We propose structured relevance determination by tying lengthscales across groups of adjacent pixels and within each colour channel. This yields patch-wise and channel-wise constrained anisotropic RBF parametrisations that reduce the number of independently learned lengthscales. We further introduce channel-additive Gaussian processes for multi-channel images and combine them with structured relevance determination, resulting in a parameter-efficient decomposition of the latent function into components defined on channel subsets, enabling some non-local generalisation. The proposed kernels are evaluated on MNIST and a compact binary aircraft-detection dataset of low-resolution RGB satellite image chips. We also show how channel-wise structured relevance determination can be incorporated into convolutional Gaussian processes. We observe improved predictive performance compared to isotropic and fully anisotropic RBF baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 论文为图像输入的高斯过程设计结构化超参数共享的 RBF 核：按相邻像素组与颜色通道绑定 lengthscale，降低全各向异性核的参数数量，并提出 channel-additive GP 把潜函数分解为定义在通道子集上的分量，在 MNIST 与低分辨率卫星图像小数据集上验证预测性能与不确定性校准的改善。
AI.relevance_reason: 其结构化 relevance determination 与通道加性潜函数分解，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据的维度筛选、patch/通道级重要性共享以及 latent 状态的分量式表示提供一条可核查的线索，但属较远的回归建模领域，与推理生成和决策的联系需进一步确认。
